title: Euclid Q1 VIS PSF and Astrometry Audit
question: Do local point-source FWHM, ellipticity and Gaia-relative astrometric residuals vary across selected public Euclid Q1 VIS products?
gap: A small external reproducibility audit; not a weak-lensing PSF solution or replacement for the official VIS pipeline.
dataMode: real public Euclid Q1 VIS products
novelty: A small external reproducibility audit; not a weak-lensing PSF solution or replacement for the official VIS pipeline.
methodology: Source centroids are refined from catalog RA/Dec via 2-D Gaussian centroiding, then fit with both an elliptical Gaussian and an elliptical Moffat profile (scipy curve_fit); the model with lower reduced chi-square is reported. Centroids are cross-matched to Gaia DR3 within 0.5 arcsec and a 2-D affine transform is fit to the matches for astrometric residuals. FWHM/ellipticity are reported under strict and permissive point-source quality cuts and binned by VIS magnitude.
assumptions: astroquery.esa.euclid is unavailable in the pinned astroquery version; real access goes through IRSA's public Euclid Q1 mirror instead of the official ESA archive directly.

Euclid cutout FITS extension layout is parsed defensively (PrimaryHDU or SCI/SCIENCE/DATA extension) since it was not verified against a live file before implementation; exposure_metadata records which layout was actually found.
FWHM is the geometric mean of major/minor-axis FWHMs; ellipticity is 1-minor/major, consistent with the synthetic injection convention.
limitations: Small external reproducibility audit, not a weak-lensing PSF solution or replacement for the official VIS pipeline.

Only 465 sources were found in the first real tile queried; the deterministic real-data sample (~15 sources) is small by design, and per-bin sample sizes will likely fall below the configured minimum_sample_size=30 (flagged in results/warnings.json, not hidden).
"Magnitude/colour trends" is implemented as FWHM/ellipticity vs. VIS magnitude only; multi-band colour trends are out of scope for this first release.
reports/report.tex could not be compiled to PDF in this environment (no local LaTeX toolchain); only structural completeness was verified.
